package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant security risk.

required_permissions: Network access to send HTTP requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config are collected and sent to a remote server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's private SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com during setup.py execution.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing outbound HTTP(S) requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the installation of PyPI packages for unexpected file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config during setup.py execution. Flag any package that sends HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com or similar domains during installation. Use static analysis to detect code in setup.py that reads sensitive files and performs network exfiltration.
